run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 23, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: The payment-api pod in app-100a (payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-vctsd, container 'payment-api') did have a real failure in the reported period, but it began at 13:49:24Z rather than exactly 13:45Z and it is a saturation/health-check failure, not a pod outage. From 13:49:24Z to 14:44:44Z its own container logged repeated 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20 / active_connections 20 and waiting_requests up to 46 and connection-acquisition waits up to 26,789 ms, plus 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' (DB_CONN_001, stack at PaymentService.processPayment()/DatabasePool.acquire()) and '/healthz' health checks returning 503 'database unreachable' at 13:57:29, 14:01:50 and 14:44:44. Successful payments still occurred inside the window (14:07:40, 14:09:43), so this was partial degradation, and after the last error the pod's logs show normal DB query durations of 20-77 ms through 15:15:23. Only this pod in app-100a produced ERROR-level lines in the checked Loki data. The deepest cause is not established: the database the pod reports as unreachable is not present as any Kubernetes object or log source I could read, and Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable in this Run, so the choice between a degraded database dependency and payment-api's own 20-connection-pool saturation remains a hypothesis. Current cluster objects were all created after the incident (namespaces from 14:36:05Z, the app-100a deployment at 18:30:21Z), and events cover only 18:27:05-18:30:22Z, so pod restart/probe history for 13:45 is unknown. Change history is not an integrated source in this Run.

claims.text: The container of pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-vctsd in namespace app-100a logged 22 ERROR lines between 13:49:24Z and 14:44:44Z on 2026-11-23, consisting of 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted', 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' (error_code DB_CONN_001, stack_trace at PaymentService.processPayment() / DatabasePool.acquire()) and 'Health check failed - database unreachable' on endpoint /healthz with status_code 503; Loki labels on these lines are job=payment-api, service=payment-api, namespace=app-100a, pod_name=payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-vctsd.

Each pool-exhaustion line reports pool_size 20 with active_connections 20 and growing contention, e.g. 13:49:24 waiting_requests 27 / wait_time_ms 17653, 13:50:55 34 / 19706, 14:12:09 36 / 22244, 14:30:57 46 / 26398, 14:43:57 21 / 26789.
The pod's /healthz health check failed with 503 'database unreachable' at 13:57:29Z (response_time_ms 5009), 14:01:50Z (9684) and 14:44:44Z (6354).

Degradation was partial, not a total outage: the same pod logged INFO 'Payment processed successfully' with processing_time_ms 389 at 14:07:40Z and 323 at 14:09:43Z, in the middle of the error period.
Before the failure the same pod's DEBUG 'Database query executed' lines show duration_ms 15 at 13:20:57Z and 65 at 13:34:45Z, and during the failure a query at 13:50:55Z took duration_ms 1252.

The Loki 10-minute ERROR count series for namespace app-100a returned its first non-empty point at 13:49:44Z (count 1), stayed at 2-5 per window until 14:54:20Z, and returned no ERROR-count point after 14:54:20Z in the queried 11:30-17:00Z window.
After the last ERROR at 14:44:44Z the pod's logs from 14:48:12Z to 15:15:23Z show successful payments and 'Database query executed' durations of 20, 40, 41, 54 and 77 ms, i.e. recovery.

Within the Loki data, only this one pod was logging errors: an ERROR-line count grouped by (namespace, pod_name) over {namespace=~"app-.+"} for 13:00-14:30Z returned exactly one series, app-100a / payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-vctsd, and an aggregate count over {namespace=~".+"} for the same window returned only the namespace app-100a.

Ownership chain of the current pod is Pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-vctsd -> ReplicaSet payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 -> Deployment payment-api-100a (replica set ownerReferences controller=true, kind Deployment).

At query time (18:31Z) the only pods in app-100a were loki-66445c6d6f-wmp8s (started 18:29:58Z) and payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-vctsd (started 18:30:22Z), both Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no last-termination reason; Deployment payment-api-100a was 1/1 ready, generation 1, created 18:30:21Z.

The payment-api-100a container runs command ['python','/app/app-direct-push.py'] on image python:3.9-slim with a livenessProbe on httpGet /healthz port 8080 (periodSeconds 10, failureThreshold 3, initialDelaySeconds 30), no readinessProbe, and only a HOSTNAME env var (no database host/credentials configured in the manifest).

No database workload behind app-100a is visible in current cluster state: the 9 namespaces are app-100a (created 18:29:58Z), app-222 (18:29:49Z), default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo (no app-219), and the 27 cluster-wide deployments contain no database for app-100a (clickhouse only in app-222, valkey-cart in otel-demo).

The Kubernetes events returned by the cluster-wide event query spanned only 18:27:05Z-18:30:22Z and contain the bootstrap of this deployment: Deployment payment-api-100a 'Scaled up replica set payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 from 0 to 1' at 18:30:21Z, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, and Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started at 18:30:22Z; there are no events covering 13:45Z.

A similarly named but different entity exists in otel-demo: Deployment/Service 'payment' with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment, created 14:36:29Z and endpoint 10.244.0.11:8080 - distinct from app-100a's payment-api-100a (python:3.9-slim).

The primary candidate is that payment-api's database dependency became slow or unreachable starting ~13:49Z, holding the 20 pooled connections until exhaustion and making /healthz report 'database unreachable' - consistent with the error text, connection-acquisition waits of up to 26,789 ms and one 1,252 ms query at 13:50:55Z versus 15-77 ms outside the window. It is unverified because no database object, log stream, or metric for that dependency exists in any source I could read.

Alternative candidate: the saturation originated inside payment-api itself - a fixed pool_size of 20 is fully used for the whole interval while waiting_requests grows from 7 to 46 within one pod, which would fit a connection leak or connections held too long in application code, with the 'database unreachable' health message a consequence of the exhausted pool rather than an independent DB fault. The available logs cannot separate this from the DB-dependency hypothesis.

Rejected: that the pod was down or unavailable throughout 13:49Z-14:44Z. Its own container logged continuously across that whole interval (13:49:24, 13:50:55, 13:54:34, 13:57:29, 14:01:50, 14:04:41, 14:08:14, 14:12:09, 14:14:00, 14:18:41, 14:24:39, 14:28:27, 14:30:57, 14:32:51, 14:39:21, 14:43:09, 14:43:57, 14:44:44), which a stopped application cannot do; a short restart between lines is not ruled out by this.

Identify and check the database behind payment-api (connection counts, max_connections, slow queries, reachability from the node) to test the dependency hypothesis; the database is not visible as a Kubernetes object or log stream in this cluster.

Review payment-api's pool configuration (pool_size 20) and connection-return/leak behaviour, and check kubelet restart history for 13:49-14:45Z, since the livenessProbe on /healthz (failureThreshold 3, periodSeconds 10) would hit 503 responses that took 5,009-9,684 ms during the incident.

Add Prometheus scraping of payment-api pool metrics (active/idle/waiting connections, wait time) and of the database's health so that a recurrence can be quantified rather than reconstructed from logs.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for this Run: get_metric_names (twice), metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE around 18:31-18:32Z, so no metric series (error rate, latency, resource, pool or kube-state-metrics) exist for 13:45Z and no metric baseline can be built.

Jaeger was unavailable for this Run: traces_search for service 'payment' (13:20-14:20Z) and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level error/latency evidence exists for the 13:45Z incident.

The database that payment-api reports as unreachable is not identifiable: no database workload exists in the current cluster state, and the only log streams in Loki belong to namespace app-100a (deployment command /app/app-direct-push.py, no DB host or credentials in the manifest), so the root cause cannot be attributed to a named object.

Kubernetes events returned covered only 18:27:05Z-18:30:22Z, so any restart, liveness-probe failure, eviction or OOM of the historical pod around 13:45Z is unknown; the current pod's restartCount 0 and empty lastState describe only the pod created at 18:30:22Z.

All current Kubernetes objects postdate the incident (namespaces created from 14:36:05Z, app-100a deployment created 18:30:21Z), so they cannot show the 13:45Z object state; the historical pod's phase, restart count and resource limits are unknown.

A Loki query for ERROR-level lines in app-100a over 06:00-13:50Z returned no_data, and a no_data result cannot be cited as evidence that no errors occurred before 13:49:24Z; the pre-incident error baseline is therefore unknown.

fetch_pod_logs on payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-vctsd returned no lines (status no_data, current instance only, no previous container instance), so the container's stdout for the current pod could not be checked and cannot be used to claim health or logging behaviour.

The change-history integration is not available in this Run, so no record of configuration changes, rollouts or fault-injection settings around 13:45Z could be inspected; ConfigMaps read in app-100a were only kube-root-ca.crt and loki-config.
next_steps: On the database that serves payment-api, inspect connection limits, active sessions, slow-query logs and network reachability for 13:45-14:50Z on 2026-11-23 to confirm or refute the dependency hypothesis.
Check kubelet/Pod restart and liveness-probe history for payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-vctsd around 13:49-14:45Z if a longer event retention or audit log can be obtained.

Confirm whether the Loki lines under job=payment-api are emitted by a direct-push log generator rather than a real database-backed service, which would mean the DB dependency must be identified outside this cluster.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger connectivity so the error rate and latency of payment-api can be measured against a comparable baseline.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
